objective: Analyzing cost/schedule/quality/risk variances against planned values and updating plans with corrective actions
secondaryObjectives: Executing program management plans and consolidating project-level data to monitor performance and communicate status
Managing program-level issues and risk per the risk management plan to protect benefits realization
Obtaining authorization through stage-gate reviews to proceed to the next program phase
Monitoring benefit metrics (forecasting, variance analysis, what-if scenarios) and taking corrective action to protect realization

sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 (through a summarizing fetch, by this round's first builder). SPI = EV / PV and CPI = EV / AC, below 1.0 meaning behind schedule and over cost for the work done. Used here for the consolidated variances of the constituent projects.

The transit authority, the program, the projects, the vendor and the people are fictional. The budget, the burn rate, the reserve, the costs of each decision, the SPI figures and the support gauges are teaching figures for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You are the program manager of the fare modernization program at Tidewater Regional Transit, a fictional transit authority. Four projects make up the program: a fare-payment app, a back-office integration, station kiosks and a data platform. The program's benefit is fare revenue collected through the app. A steering committee meets monthly and holds the program reserve.
handover: Program budget: 6,000 thousand dollars, including a 300 thousand dollar reserve the steering committee controls. Planned spend is about 1,400 thousand dollars a month.
The risk management plan sends any risk that threatens a program benefit to the steering committee. Stage gates are authorized by the committee.
howItWorks: The board shows the program's risk register against its appetite, each stakeholder's support in words, the budget committed and the steering docket.
Move the program on a month at a time. A decision comes to you at each steering review; before the first, you can consolidate the projects' data or read the registers.
After month 5 you write the program status record and a short reflection.

statusPrompt.title: Month 1: the first steering review
statusPrompt.context: The four project managers send their reports: fare app green, back-office integration amber, station kiosks green, data platform green. Their schedule data, put side by side, show the integration project at SPI 0.82, and the kiosk installs start next month on stations that need the integration's links.

choices.label: Consolidate the four projects' data into one program view, show the integration variance and its effect on the kiosks, and propose the corrective action: re-sequence the kiosk installs after integration and move two developers from the fare app

effects.log: The committee approves the re-sequencing; the integration plan is updated.

choices.feedback: Program status is consolidated from the components' data, variances are analyzed across their interdependencies, and corrective action updates the plan.

choices.label: Pass the four RAG reports to the committee as the program status
choices.feedback: Four separate reports hide the interdependency: the kiosks are green only until they need the integration's links.

choices.label: Take over the integration project's plan yourself and add a second vendor team on overtime to catch up

effects.log: You re-plan the integration over its project manager's head and book an overtime team.

choices.feedback: The program manager directs components through their project managers and the plan; taking over a project and adding unplanned spend bypasses both.

riskPrompt.title: Month 2: the certification risk moves above the program's appetite
riskPrompt.context: The payment processor's certification queue is now six weeks; the fare app's slot is at the end of month 3, with no retest before next quarter. The risk management plan says risks that threaten a program benefit go to the steering committee, which holds a 300 thousand dollar reserve. A second test lab (250 thousand) would let the team pre-test.

choices.label: Escalate it to the steering committee as the risk management plan says, with the options and their effect on the fare revenue benefit; recommend the second lab from the program reserve

effects.log: The committee funds the second lab from the reserve and records the decision.

choices.feedback: Program risks that threaten benefits are escalated to the level that owns them, with options, and treated by the plan's response.

choices.label: Leave it with the fare-app project team; certification is a project matter

effects.log: The risk stays at project level.

choices.feedback: A risk that threatens a program benefit is a program risk; leaving it in one project leaves it untreated.

choices.label: Cut the kiosk project's scope by a third to free 250 thousand dollars and fund the lab now, without waiting for the committee

effects.log: You cut another project's scope on your own authority.

choices.feedback: Re-scoping a component and moving its money is the committee's decision, not the program manager's.

gatePrompt.title: Month 3: the stage gate to deployment
gatePrompt.context: The gate's three criteria: integration tests passed, certification passed, operations staff trained. The first two are met; training is 60% done and scheduled to finish in three weeks. Deployment is planned to start next week.

choices.label: Present the gate pack as it stands and ask the committee to authorize deployment on condition that training finishes before any station goes live, with a date

effects.log: Authorized with one condition, recorded with its date.

choices.feedback: Authorization to proceed comes from the governance body at the gate; an unmet criterion is presented with a condition and a date.

choices.label: Declare the gate passed yourself; two of three is close enough and the schedule matters

effects.log: Deployment starts without the committee's authorization.

choices.feedback: Passing a gate is the governance body's decision; the program manager prepares and recommends.

choices.label: Postpone the gate a month until every criterion is met

effects.log: The gate moves a month; the deployment crews stand by at 100 thousand dollars.

choices.feedback: Waiting is safe but costs a month and money; a conditional authorization would have kept the plan.

benefitPrompt.title: Month 4: fare-app adoption is below the benefits plan
benefitPrompt.context: The benefits realization plan expects 35% of fares paid through the app by the end of the year. Adoption is 22% after six weeks; the forecast on the current trend is 26%. Operations, the benefit owner, says station staff were never asked to promote the app.

choices.label: Analyze the variance with the benefit owner, agree a corrective action (station staff promotion and a first-ride offer, 40 thousand dollars), forecast its effect, and update the benefits register and the sponsor

effects.log: Forecast after the campaign: 33%. The benefits register shows the variance, the action and the owner.

choices.feedback: Benefit metrics are monitored against the plan; a variance gets analysis, a forecast and corrective action with the benefit owner.

choices.label: Change the target in the benefits register to 26% so the program reports on plan

effects.log: The register now says 26%; the business case still says 35%.

choices.feedback: Moving the target to the forecast hides the variance from the people who approved the business case.

choices.label: Note it for the program closure report
choices.feedback: Benefits are protected during the program, while there is time to act, not reported after it.

reflection.question: Write the program status note for the steering committee: how the program performed against its plan and what you corrected, and how the risk, the gate and the benefits variance were handled.

parts.label: Variances and corrective action
parts.criteria: Consolidates the projects' data, reads the integration's SPI of 0.82 and its effect on the kiosks, and names the corrective action that updated the plan.
parts.modelAnswer: Put together, the projects' data showed integration at SPI 0.82 with the kiosks waiting on it; we re-sequenced the kiosk installs and moved two developers, and integration recovered.

parts.label: Risk, gate and benefits
parts.criteria: The certification risk went to the committee under the risk plan; the gate was authorized by the committee with a condition; the adoption variance got analysis, corrective action and an updated register.
parts.modelAnswer: Certification threatened the fare benefit, so it went to the committee, which funded a second lab from the reserve. The committee authorized deployment on condition training finished first. Adoption was 22% against 35%; with operations we ran a staff promotion and forecast 33%.

expertPath.text: Consolidate the projects' data and read the registers.
Show the integration variance and its effect on the kiosks; re-sequence and move two developers.

authority.headline: Not your decision to take
authority.body: Gates are authorized and components re-scoped by the governance body. The program manager analyzes, recommends and escalates.

materialized.headline: The risk to the benefit was left in a project
materialized.body: A risk that threatens a program benefit belongs at program level and, under this plan, with the steering committee.

overspend.headline: Over budget
overspend.body: Unplanned spend to catch up a project is a decision for the plan and the committee, not a fix the program manager books.

steered.headline: Good: steered on the plan, within authority
steered.body: Consolidated variances drove corrective action, the risk went to its owner, the gate to the committee and the benefit variance to the benefit owner.

drifted.headline: Delivered, with gaps
drifted.body: The criteria show which review was missed: the consolidated status, the gate, or the benefits variance.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: The record was not written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: A program manager monitors performance by consolidating the components' data: four green and amber reports hid that the kiosks depended on an integration project at SPI 0.82, so the corrective action re-sequenced the kiosks and moved capacity. A risk that threatens a program benefit is a program risk, escalated as the risk management plan says to the committee that holds the reserve. A stage gate is authorized by the governance body; an unmet criterion is presented with a condition and a date. Benefit metrics are tracked against the realization plan; a variance gets analysis with the benefit owner, a corrective action and a forecast, and the register keeps the original target.
